title: Josh Kushner raised $2bn to buy the companies AI is coming for
excerpt: Thrive Holdings raised $2bn at a $12bn valuation from SoftBank. It buys accounting and IT firms outright, then puts its own AI engineers inside.
content_html:
Almost every AI business sells a product. Someone builds a model or a tool, licenses it, and hopes the customer works out what to do with it.

Thrive Holdings inverts that. It buys accounting firms and IT services companies outright, puts its own engineers inside them, and rebuilds how the work gets done. It now owns more than 70 businesses.

On Wednesday it said it had raised more than $2bn in new capital at a $12bn valuation. The New York Times reported it first. Total capital raised since inception now passes $3bn.

The first outside money it has taken

SoftBank Group, D1 Capital Partners and Altimeter Capital led the round. Until now Thrive Holdings had run on roughly $1bn in commitments from Thrive Capital’s own institutional base, Tech Funding News reported. This is the first time outside investors have backed the vehicle.

Kushner spun Thrive Holdings out of Thrive Capital in 2025. The parent firm is 16 years old, backs OpenAI, Stripe and SpaceX, and closed a $10bn fund in February.

Read the spinout as a change of view rather than a side project. Kushner already owns pieces of the companies building AI. This vehicle buys the ones that will have to use it.

SoftBank’s presence carries its own signal. Masayoshi Son has said that calling AI a bubble is an insult.

What the 70 businesses actually do

Current is the accounting arm. It has grown to more than 50 firms and over 2,000 professionals. Shield is the IT arm, at around 20 companies.

Neither category is glamorous, and that is the point. Thrive says it looks for markets that are large, fragmented, mission-critical and operationally complex. Accounting and IT support fit all four.

The performance numbers are striking. Current’s tax agents, branded TaxAI, have processed more than 7,000 returns at 98% accuracy and cut preparation time by over 30%. Shield says its tools have sped up help desk resolution by 36 times, and that custom agent deployments roughly doubled in the past month.

Every one of those figures comes from Thrive. None is audited, and none has a published baseline. A 36-fold speed-up is a ratio without a starting number, and 98% accuracy on a tax return does not say what counts as a miss.

The third platform is really about permits

Part of the money funds a new vertical, and it is the most interesting line in the announcement. Thrive is going after the regulatory work behind physical assets, which means permits, inspections, technical documentation and compliance tracking.

The targets it names are data centres, manufacturing, healthcare, power, water and transport.

“The US needs to build and modernize more critical infrastructure, but projects are often constrained by local, technical, and regulatory complexity,” founding member Anuj Mehndiratta told TechCrunch.

That constraint is real, and it is getting worse. More than 500 US towns now restrict or ban data centres.

Kareem Zaki, another founding member, framed the pitch as compression. AI working alongside practitioners can “compress regulatory bottlenecks, keep the safety standards high, but also be able to do it with less of a burden”, he said.

Mehndiratta was careful about the limits, which is worth noting. AI will not replace field work, local judgement or professional sign-off, he said.

OpenAI is inside the machine

The relationship that makes this model work is not incidental. OpenAI took an ownership stake in Thrive Holdings in December 2025, and the deal sent OpenAI employees to work directly inside Thrive’s portfolio companies.

Thrive Capital is also one of OpenAI’s largest backers. So OpenAI owns part of a company spun out of a firm that owns part of OpenAI.

The AI economy keeps producing this shape. Lambda borrowed $917m to buy chips from a company that invests in it.

SoftBank sits in the loop too. It is one of OpenAI’s largest investors, and it has now bought into a business whose competitive edge is OpenAI staff on secondment.

Three firms, one bet

Thrive is not alone in this. OpenAI built DeployCo with TPG and Bain Capital, a joint venture worth $10bn. Anthropic built Ode with Blackstone.

All three put engineers inside client organisations rather than selling licences. The wager is identical: the money is in implementation, not in the model.

The roll-up version is spreading as well. Beacon raised $225m for an AI roll-up of its own.

What separates Thrive is ownership. DeployCo and Ode work for their clients. Thrive owns them, so it keeps the margin instead of billing for it.

None of this is European

That is worth saying plainly. The announcement is about America, and Thrive says it wants to make it easier to modernise and build America’s physical infrastructure. It names no European market at all.

The model would travel. European accountancy and IT support are at least as fragmented as their American equivalents, and European permitting is not famously quick.

What Europe lacks is the buyer. This requires a fund willing to purchase hundreds of small professional firms outright and then run them, which is a different animal from a venture fund writing cheques into startups.

The number was public five months ago

This raise surprised nobody who was reading. Tech Funding News reported in March that Thrive Holdings was in talks for “at least $2 billion”. It closed in August at exactly that.

The company’s own announcement reads unusually for a startup. It carries a securities-style disclaimer warning that its statements are forward-looking and that “actual results may differ materially”.

That is the language of a firm that expects to be quoted back to itself.

What would settle it

Two things are checkable. The first is whether any operating number ever gets confirmed by a customer or an auditor rather than by the owner.

The second is whether the permitting platform ships at all. Accounting and IT are workflows Thrive controls end to end, and it can rewrite them because it owns them.

A permit is different. It is a decision made by somebody who does not work for Thrive, in a town that did not ask for a data centre, and no amount of compute changes who signs it.

content_html_zh:
几乎每个人工智能企业都销售一种产品。 有人构建了一个模型或工具，对其进行许可，并希望客户弄清楚如何使用它。

Thrive Holdings 扭转了这一局面。 它直接收购了会计师事务所和 IT 服务公司，将自己的工程师放入其中，并重建了工作的完成方式。 目前拥有70多家企业。

周三，该公司表示已筹集超过 20 亿美元的新资本，估值为 120 亿美元。 《纽约时报》率先报道了此事。 自成立以来筹集的总资金现已超过 30 亿美元。

它拿走的第一笔外部资金

软银集团、D1 Capital Partners 和 Altimeter Capital 领投此轮融资。 据 Tech Funding News 报道，到目前为止，Thrive Holdings 已经从 Thrive Capital 自己的机构基础上获得了大约 10 亿美元的承诺。 这是外部投资者首次支持该工具。

库什纳于 2025 年将 Thrive Holdings 从 Thrive Capital 中剥离出来。 其母公司已有 16 年历史，支持 OpenAI、Stripe 和 SpaceX，并于 2 月份关闭了一只 100 亿美元的基金。

将衍生产品视为观点的改变，而不是一个副项目。 库什纳已经拥有人工智能公司的部分股份。 这辆车购买那些必须使用它的人。

软银的存在本身就带有信号。 孙正义表示，称人工智能为泡沫是一种侮辱。

70 家企业实际做什么

目前是会计部门。 它已发展到拥有 50 多家公司和 2,000 多名专业人员。 Shield 是大约 20 家公司的 IT 部门。

这两个类别都不迷人，但这就是重点。 Thrive 表示，它正在寻找大型、分散、任务关键且运营复杂的市场。 会计和 IT 支持满足这四个条件。

性能数据令人震惊。 Current 的税务代理（品牌为 TaxAI）已处理了 7,000 多份申报表，准确率达 98%，并将准备时间缩短了 30% 以上。 Shield 表示，其工具已将帮助台解决问题的速度提高了 36 倍，并且自定义代理部署量在过去一个月中大约增加了一倍。

这些数字中的每一个都来自 Thrive。 没有一个经过审计，也没有一个已发布的基线。 36 倍的加速是一个没有起始数字的比率，纳税申报表上 98% 的准确率并不能说明什么算作失误。

第三个平台实际上是关于许可证的

部分资金资助了一个新的垂直领域，这是公告中最有趣的一行。 Thrive 正在开展实物资产背后的监管工作，这意味着许可证、检查、技术文档和合规跟踪。

它指定的目标是数据中心、制造、医疗保健、电力、水和交通。

“美国需要建设和现代化更关键的基础设施，但项目往往受到当地、技术和监管复杂性的限制，”创始成员 Anuj Mehndiratta 告诉 TechCrunch。

这种限制是真实存在的，而且越来越严重。 目前，美国 500 多个城镇限制或禁止数据中心。

另一位创始成员卡里姆·扎基 (Kareem Zaki) 将此次推介视为压缩。 他说，人工智能与从业者一起工作可以“压缩监管瓶颈，保持高安全标准，而且还能减轻负担”。

值得注意的是，曼迪拉塔对限制很谨慎。 他说，人工智能不会取代现场工作、当地判断或专业签字。

OpenAI 位于机器内部

使这个模型发挥作用的关系并非偶然。 OpenAI 于 2025 年 12 月获得了 Thrive Holdings 的所有权，这笔交易让 OpenAI 员工直接在 Thrive 的投资组合公司内部工作。

Thrive Capital 也是 OpenAI 最大的支持者之一。 因此，OpenAI 拥有一家公司的一部分，该公司是从一家拥有 OpenAI 部分的公司分拆出来的。

人工智能经济不断产生这种形状。 Lambda 借了 9.17 亿美元从投资它的公司购买芯片。

软银也参与其中。 它是OpenAI最大的投资者之一，现在已经收购了一家以OpenAI借调员工为竞争优势的企业。

三家公司，一赌

Thrive 并不孤单。 OpenAI 与 TPG 和 Bain Capital 建立了 DeployCo，这是一家价值 100 亿美元的合资企业。 Anthropic 与 Blackstone 共同打造了 Ode。

这三者都将工程师安置在客户组织内，而不是出售许可证。 赌注是相同的：钱是在实施中，而不是在模型中。

卷起版本也正在传播。 Beacon 筹集了 2.25 亿美元用于自己的人工智能业务。

Thrive 的区别在于所有权。 DeployCo 和 Ode 为他们的客户服务。 Thrive 拥有它们，因此它可以保留利润而不是收取费用。

这些都不是欧洲的

这值得直白地说。 该公告是关于美国的，Thrive 表示，它希望让美国的实体基础设施的现代化和建设变得更加容易。 它根本没有提到欧洲市场。

模型会旅行。 欧洲的会计和 IT 支持至少与美国的同行一样分散，而且欧洲的许可速度也不是出了名的快。

欧洲缺少的是买家。 这需要一支愿意直接购买数百家小型专业公司然后运营它们的基金，这与向初创企业开支票的风险基金是不同的。

这个数字是五个月前公开的

这次加薪没有让正在阅读的人感到惊讶。 Tech Fund News 3 月份报道称，Thrive Holdings 正在就“至少 20 亿美元”进行谈判。 它于八月恰好在那个时间关闭。

对于一家初创公司来说，该公司自己的公告读起来不同寻常。 它带有证券式的免责声明，警告其声明具有前瞻性，并且“实际结果可能存在重大差异”。

这是一家希望自己被引用的公司的语言。

什么可以解决它

有两件事是可以检查的。 第一个是任何运营号码是否由客户或审计员而不是业主确认。

第二个问题是获得许可的平台是否真的可以发货。 会计和 IT 是 Thrive 端到端控制的工作流程，它可以重写它们，因为它拥有它们。

许可证不同。 这是由一个不为 Thrive 工作的人做出的决定，在一个不需要数据中心的小镇上，签署该决定的人也没有进行任何计算更改。
